vitalis-bio.name: Vitalis Bio
vitalis-bio.summary: Turn your wearable and lab data into a dynamic biological age score and reverse your aging curve. Upload any lab PDF, get a biological age you can audit,

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: They built the thing that survives the no-budget, no-internet, no-permission case.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: Turn your wearable and lab data into a dynamic biological age score and reverse your aging curve. Upload any lab PDF, get a biological age you can audit,
steal_this: Find the metric practitioners already eyeball, instrument it, and ship the delta. A number turns a vibe into a product.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A chatbot answering questions nobody asked mid-task. — then Vitalis Bio made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any product whose users hate forms

audit.worth_note: Two pieces are worth taking and one is worth doubting. Grammar-constrained decoding for provider-specific PDF layouts is a real technique for any document pipeline, and smoothing volatile wearable inputs with nested EMAs before feeding a scoring model is the unglamorous fix that makes a score stable enough to display. The product itself sits in a crowded longevity-dashboard category whose hardest part - whether the number means anything - is exactly where the page offers a percentage with no denominator.

artifact_exists.why: no source repo linked, but the page publishes a working artifact: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sYupP9m-aqE

build_is_real.why: no repository published, so the build cannot be read

limits_disclosed.why: no limitations section, but 'what's next' implies the open edges

numbers_add_up.why: 3 figure(s) a reader can check against the product (nine biomarkers in the PhenoAge clock; two-tap onboarding to a baseline clock), but 1 headline figure(s) carry no testable denominator: over 95% accuracy parsing lab PDFs

stack_consistency.why: no repo to cross-check the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.why: a figure with a stated denominator is quoted, but the capture records no harness, held-out set or method behind it

assumptions: you accept an existing clinical formula rather than fitting your own, so coefficients are copied from a paper
you have users willing to connect real blood panels, since without panels the score is wearable noise
no regulatory clearance is implied; a consumer dashboard, not a diagnostic device
clone_cost.estimate: about a week for the pipeline, longer for anything you would defend clinically
clone_cost.why: Reading the published PhenoAge formula and applying nine lab values is a day's work; HealthKit and Health Connect auth plus a Gemini schema-constrained PDF pass is another few. The part that does not come free is a labelled corpus to know your parser is right, and any claim about reversing aging.

audit.what_to_steal: Force the extraction model into a strict response schema per provider instead of writing per-provider parsers, and keep the raw values alongside the parsed ones; smooth noisy physiological inputs over a short and a long window so a derived score cannot jitter day to day; ship the derived score against a baseline the user already trusts (chronological age) rather than as a bare number.
audit.what_breaks_first: Trust in the score, the moment it moves for a reason the user can see is unrelated to their behaviour. A PhenoAge output is dominated by blood chemistry that changes quarterly, while the weekly loop promises movement from sleep and steps, so the dashboard's cadence and the model's sensitivity disagree; the reported parsing accuracy cannot rescue it either, since a single misread unit becomes a wrong age.

prior_art.relation: same architecture of trust - a published clinical score presented through a calm UI with an escalation-style recommendation loop - and the same unmeasured gap between a computed index and validated guidance.

opposite end of the same problem: Medvoice closes a loop on an action the patient confirms, while this one opens a recommendation loop with no adherence signal at all. Comparing them shows what a verification step buys.

hazard.note: A biological-age score computed from a mortality model, presented to consumers with weekly supplement and protocol recommendations, and a roadmap that plans to predict how interventions shift the curve. Nothing on the page frames the output as non-medical, and no clinician review, cohort or validation is mentioned for the score its interface is built around.

neuroguard-ai-adaptiveconcussionrecovery.name: NeuroGuard AI
neuroguard-ai-adaptiveconcussionrecovery.summary: Turns daily concussion symptoms into clear, evidence-grounded recovery guidance and timely safety escalation for patients, caregivers, and clinicians.

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: The team treated the annoying part of the workflow as the product, not the demo.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: Turns daily concussion symptoms into clear, evidence-grounded recovery guidance and timely safety escalation for patients, caregivers, and clinicians.
steal_this: Decide which single action is expensive enough to require a human, and make that gate a schema state transition rather than a prompt request.
Anything the architecture can enforce, the architecture enforces. Probabilistic components get proposals; deterministic components get verdicts.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A chatbot answering questions nobody asked mid-task. — then NeuroGuard AI made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any product whose users hate forms

audit.worth_note: The architecture is the contribution: deterministic extraction, rule-based history-aware scoring, retrieval over a guideline corpus, and escalation that pre-empts advice - with the generative model kept out of the decision path. That is the correct shape for software that touches a regulated outcome, and it is rare to see it chosen deliberately at hackathon scale. Held below breakthrough because the pieces are standard practice in clinical decision support.

artifact_exists.why: no source repo linked, but the page publishes a working artifact: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6VTxPCeStvo

build_is_real.why: no repository published, so the build cannot be read

limits_disclosed.why: no limitations section, but 'what's next' implies the open edges

numbers_add_up.why: 1 figure(s) a reader can check against the product (five-stage recovery plan), but 1 headline figure(s) carry no testable denominator: 100% accuracy across the included evaluation cases

stack_consistency.why: no repo to cross-check the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.why: a measured evaluation with a stated denominator is described on the page (an A/B comparison or a logged-outcome harness counts; a bare 'we tested it' does not)

assumptions: you may legally embed the guideline text you retrieve from
a clinician reviews the escalation thresholds before anyone relies on them
no diagnosis or treatment claim is made in your copy
clone_cost.estimate: 1 week for the check-in core, 3-4 weeks with history, handoff and a real eval
clone_cost.why: FastAPI, SQLite, Pydantic and local retrieval are ordinary parts; the work is the guideline corpus, the rule set and the evaluation cases

audit.what_to_steal: Escalation precedence: compute the red-flag rules first and *suppress* the normal path when they fire, rather than letting a friendly assistant narrate its way past a warning sign. Pair it with schema validation of every structured result before it renders, and hand the professional a summary artifact rather than a chat transcript.
audit.what_breaks_first: The self-graded benchmark: 100% across a case set nobody outside the team defined or counted measures their agreement with themselves, and the page is honest enough to say it is not clinical validation - so a clone inherits the need for a real evaluation with data and a clinician. Second, multi-day history with no persistence story (secure cross-session storage is still on the roadmap).

prior_art.relation: parallel invention at the same event under the same name: baseline-relative monitoring, no rules, no retrieval - keep both, and note this one is specified far more tightly
same containment pattern elsewhere: bounded evidence requests and one human-approved mutation step
same 'cite the rule the verdict came from' discipline applied to a different regulated document type

hazard.note: Risk assessment on a medical condition. The team disclaims diagnosis, states the benchmarks are not clinical validation, and keeps recommendations conservative; that is better hygiene than most of the corpus, not permission to run it on real patients without oversight.
